correctness.rationale: For odd \(n\), the source's unique positive-definite regular-family member has \(j=(n-1)/2\), \(\theta=\alpha=\pi/n\), and, after simplification, invariant form proportional to \(Q=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,v^2(2v+1))\) with \(v=\cos\alpha\). For consecutive Euclidean side midpoints \(M_k\), direct symbolic reconstruction gives \(\langle M_k,M_{k+1}\rangle_Q/\langle M_k,M_k\rangle_Q=v\). Thus normalized consecutive lifts subtend the minor spherical angle \(\arccos v=\alpha\), and the primitive \(n\)-bounce midpoint orbit has exact total length \(n\alpha=\pi\). The source supplies openness of the strict midpoint witness and the spherical metric-rigidity congruence; continuity on a connected periodic component then makes length locally constant in the discrete class \(\pi+2\pi\mathbb Z\), so the component containing the witness has exact length \(\pi\). The conclusion is correctly limited to that connected component.
residual_risks: The theorem does not classify other connected periodic components or indefinite members of the projective family.
